intro: The wind has been at the river notice board. Marek holds a handful of torn strips. 'Three notices, all in pieces, and the ferry crowd is waiting to read them. Each notice had a claim, the evidence for it, and a line saying where it stops. Put them back together.'

pieces.text: The ferry leaves at dawn every day.
The north well is safe to drink from.
The flood will reach the bottom step by the new moon.
The ferry log shows a dawn crossing on 28 of the last 30 days.
Two tests this month found the water clear and sweet.
In each of the last five years, the flood reached the bottom step within ten days of the first rise.
Everyone on the quay says so.
The log does not say why the other two days had no crossing.
Both tests were made before the river rose.
This year's first rise was smaller than in any of those five years.

rumour: Marek holds the strip up to the light. 'Everyone on the quay says so. That tells us who believes it. It does not tell us why. Put it aside.'
wrong: Nasir lays the two strips side by side. 'This one is about {a}, and that one is about {b}. They tore from different notices.'
fixed: The notice about {about} holds together again: what it says, why, and where it stops.
orderAsk: Nasir smooths the three notices flat. 'One more thing. On the board, which line goes at the top? The crowd reads the top line and walks on.'

claim.marek: 'Good. People need to know what we are telling them. The limit is there for anyone who reads to the end.'
claim.nasir: 'And most people will not read to the end. They will carry the claim away without its limit, and the well will be safe until somebody is sick.'

limit.marek: 'Then nobody knows what the notice is about until the second line. A warning nobody understands warns nobody.'
limit.nasir: 'But the limit is what changes since last week. The river rose. That is the news a reader needs first.'

evidence.marek: 'Fair. Start from what we saw, and let the reader make the claim. That is how I would want to be told.'
evidence.nasir: 'It is fair, and it is slow. A ferry crowd will read "28 of the last 30 days" and not know what question it answers.'

close: The three notices go back up, pinned at all four corners this time. Marek ties down a spare strip at the bottom: 'If you know something these notices do not, write it here.'
